blocks.text: Words you will hear on your first shift

headers: What it means in one line
rows: The phone telling the network: I am here, let me in.
The data session once the phone is attached - the pipe for internet.
Which network the phone wants to use, e.g. internet or mms.
The SIM permanent ID number (15 digits, starts 65001 for TNM).
The phone number. Stays the same even if the SIM swaps.
The database that holds every subscriber profile.

The node that handles the user actual traffic and gives them an IP.

A live log of what one subscriber did on the network - your best debugging tool.

blocks.text: The five most useful commands, and what they tell you

blocks.title: 1. Is the subscriber attached, and on what network?
blocks.notes: This is the very first thing you run. It tells you whether the subscriber is even on the network, and which RAT (2G, 3G, 4G) they are using right now.
blocks.on_failure: If it returns no record, the subscriber is not attached. Check the SIM, the phone, and the HSS profile before doing anything else.

blocks.title: 2. Does the subscriber profile have the right APN?
blocks.notes: The GPRS profile on the HSS lists every APN the subscriber is allowed to use. If the APN they are trying to reach is not in this list, they cannot get data.
blocks.on_failure: If the APN is missing, you will need to add it - see the APN Provisioning module. Do NOT add it without a change ticket.

blocks.title: 3. Are any of the subscriber services locked?
blocks.notes: Any service listed as TRUE is locked - usually because of unpaid billing, a fraud flag, or a customer request. A locked service blocks data even when everything else looks fine.
blocks.on_failure: If something is TRUE, it is not a network problem - it is a billing or customer-service matter. Escalate, do not fix it yourself.

blocks.title: 4. Is the subscriber 4G-enabled?
blocks.notes: On LTE, the subscriber SIM must be EPS-enabled to attach. If this comes back empty, the subscriber cannot use 4G at all - even if their phone is fine.
blocks.on_failure: If not EPS-enabled, provision EPS in the HSS (with a change ticket), then ask the customer to re-attach.

blocks.title: 5. Is the UGW giving the subscriber a session?
blocks.code:
DSP CPPDPCTXT;   // on the CGW (control)
DSP UPPDPCTXT;    // on the DGW (data)
blocks.notes: These two commands show the PDP context on the gateway side. If the subscriber is attached but has no traffic, this is where you check whether the gateway actually built the session.
blocks.on_failure: If both volumes are zero, the session never established. Enable a trace and see where it fails - usually a policy or charging rejection.

modules.title: Purpose, Scope & Operational Rules
modules.subtitle: Standard Operating Procedure - PS Core Networks.

blocks.text: Purpose

This SOP collects the working knowledge, procedures and lessons learned for PS Core operations. It helps engineers understand the PS Core environment, run routine checks, troubleshoot subscriber and network problems, carry out approved configuration and provisioning work, monitor network performance, and escalate issues with enough technical evidence.
Scope

Covers the PS Core environment supporting 2G, 3G, and 4G packet-switched services. Includes topology, protocols, subscriber identification, attach and PDP procedures, static routing, APN provisioning, KPIs and alarms, troubleshooting and tracing, Huawei support and ticket escalation, CHR and Health Check collection, license management, and roaming.
General Operational Rules

blocks.title: Rules You Must Follow
items: Use only approved commands, scripts, tools, and procedures.
Never change production configuration without authorization.
Record subscriber, APN, node, time, and symptom before troubleshooting.
Keep screenshots, traces, CHR, and Health Check as evidence.
Protect subscriber information at all times.
Confirm commands against the current software version.

blocks.text: Approval

items.question: Before you start troubleshooting, what should you record?
options: Nothing until you have found the cause
Subscriber, APN, node, time and symptom
items.explain: This is one of the General Operational Rules.

items.question: When may you change production configuration?
items.explain: Never change production configuration without authorization.

items.question: What should you do after every change?
options: Nothing; the command output is enough
items.explain: Verify after every change.

items.question: What should you keep as evidence?
options: Screenshots, traces, CHR and Health Check
items.explain: Keep them so the work can be reviewed and escalated.

modules.title: Subscriber Identification: IMSI
modules.subtitle: How the EPC identifies a subscriber.

blocks.text: The International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) is a 15-digit number the EPC uses to identify a subscriber. It can change during a SIM swap, but the MSISDN (phone number) stays the same.
Structure

rows: Starts with 01; last 8 digits come from the physical SIM

blocks.title: Reading an IMSI
blocks.text: 650 01 0114416xx  →  Malawi / TNM / subscriber 0114416xx. The last 8 digits are printed on the card.

blocks.title: Where the IMSI is used
items: Routing behind MS config on CGW
All session contexts on USN and UGW
Traces across S1-MME, S6a, S11, S5/S8, Gx, Gy

blocks.title: SIM swap
blocks.text: When a customer does a SIM swap, the IMSI changes but the MSISDN stays the same. Update static routes on the CGW and any HSS profile entries.

items.question: How many digits does an IMSI have?
items.explain: It is a 15-digit number: MCC (3) + MNC (2) + MSIN (10).

items.question: In a TNM IMSI such as 650 01 0114416xx, which part identifies the country?
items.explain: 650 is the Mobile Country Code for Malawi.

items.question: A customer does a SIM swap. What happens?
options: The IMSI changes and the MSISDN stays the same
The MSISDN changes and the IMSI stays the same
items.explain: Update static routes on the CGW and any HSS profile entries.

modules.title: Key Protocols: GTP & Diameter
modules.subtitle: The two protocol families that do most of the work.

blocks.text: Two protocols do almost all the signalling and traffic work in the PS Core: GTP (tunnels subscriber data and mobility signalling) and Diameter (carries authentication, policy, and charging between USN, HSS, UPCF, and CBS via the DRA).
3.1  GTP: GPRS Tunnelling Protocol

rows: Control plane: creates / updates / deletes PDP contexts and EPS bearers, handles handovers
User plane: carries the subscriber's actual IP traffic once a session is established

blocks.title: Why split GTP-C and GTP-U?
blocks.text: Separating control from user plane lets CGW and DGW scale independently.
3.2  Diameter Protocol

rows: Fetch and update subscriber profile during attach and mobility events
Install and enforce Policy and Charging Control (PCC) rules

blocks.title: TNM Realm
blocks.text: epc.mnc650.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org is routed via the LMB and LLG DRAs, with master/slave failover.

items.question: Which GTP variant carries the subscriber's actual IP traffic?
items.explain: GTP-U is the user plane. GTP-C is the control plane.

items.question: Which Diameter interface sits between the USN and the HSS?
items.explain: S6a fetches and updates the subscriber profile during attach and mobility events.

items.question: Which interface lets the UGW get policy (PCC) rules from the UPCF?
items.explain: Gx installs and enforces Policy and Charging Control rules.

items.question: Why are GTP-C and GTP-U kept separate?
options: So the HSS can authenticate faster
So the CGW and DGW can scale independently
items.explain: Separating control from user plane lets them scale independently.

modules.title: Attach & PDP Session Establishment
modules.subtitle: How a subscriber gets on the network and gets a data session.

blocks.text: LTE Attach Procedure (4G)

blocks.caption: LTE Attach flow: UE, eNodeB, USN (MME/SGW), UGW (PGW), HSS, UPCF

rows: UE sends IMSI to eNodeB, forwarded to USN (MME) over S1-AP
USN registers location with HSS; HSS returns profile
USN instructs UGW (SGW) to create session
UGW (PGW) allocates IP, returns via SGW to USN
USN sends Attach Accept to eNodeB
UE confirms attach; eNodeB relays to USN
USN confirms eNodeB tunnel endpoint to UGW

blocks.text: PDP Context Activation (2G/3G)

blocks.caption: PDP Context Activation: UE, USN (SGSN), HSS, UGW (GGSN), UPCF, CBS

rows: UE requests activation with APN, QoS, NSAPI
USN (SGSN) requests PDP context from UGW (GGSN)
UGW (GGSN) requests PCC rules from UPCF
UGW (GGSN) allocates IP, returns to USN (SGSN)

items.question: In an LTE attach, which message registers the subscriber's location with the HSS?
items.explain: The USN registers location with the HSS, and the HSS returns the profile.

items.question: In an LTE attach, which node allocates the IP address?
items.explain: The UGW (PGW) allocates the IP and returns it via the SGW to the USN.

items.question: In a 2G/3G PDP context activation, which interface does the UGW (GGSN) use to request credit from the CBS?
items.explain: Gy is the charging authorization step.

modules.title: Roaming (LTE / GSM / GPRS)
modules.subtitle: Enable and verify inbound / outbound roaming.

blocks.caption: Inbound LTE Roaming: USN & DRA signalling and user-plane path
MOD PLMNRSZI with PROV=FALSE: enables roaming
MOD PLMNRSZI with PROV=TRUE: withdraws the roaming template

blocks.title: GSM: verify IMSI prefix on both MSC nodes
CAMEL: verify prefix on both MSC nodes
LTE: add Diameter route
blocks.code: ADD DMRT: ROUTEIDX=53, ISDEFAULT=NO, RSELMODE=SELMODE_MASTER_SLAVE, REALMNAME="epc.mnc004.mcc204.3gppnetwork.org", PEERIDX=6, ROUTENAM="NLDLT", PRIORITY=1;

blocks.title: DRA priorities
blocks.text: LLG USN: LLG DRA highest (PEERIDX 7, Priority 0). LMB USN: LMB DRA highest (PEERIDX 6, Priority 0).

blocks.title: LTE Roaming Configuration Checklist
items: Test call tracing confirms ULR → HSS and ULA returned

items.question: To enable LTE roaming with MOD PLMNRSZI, what do you set PROV to?
items.explain: PROV=FALSE enables roaming; PROV=TRUE disables it.

items.question: What do you need from the roaming partner before you start?
items.explain: It is the first item on the roaming checklist.

items.question: At the LLG USN, which DRA has the highest priority?
items.explain: LLG USN: LLG DRA highest (PEERIDX 7, Priority 0).

items.question: Which command verifies the GPRS IMSI prefix on the USN?
items.explain: LST IMSIGT with IMSIPRE.

blocks.title: Determine the scope
items: Is it everyone, a region, an APN, or one subscriber?

items: Confirm the affected subscriber's IMSI and MSISDN
Confirm the APN they are trying to reach
Confirm the affected node (USN, UGW, HSS)
Record the exact time of occurrence

blocks.title: Node and profile checks
items: Check subscriber provisioning in HSS (LST OPTGPRS, LST EPS, LST SUB)
Check relevant PS Core node status (USN, UGW)
Check active alarms on USN, UGW, HSS
Check relevant KPIs on DataPlus / U2020
Check subscriber / session context (DSP SMCTXT, DSP CPPDPCTXT, DSP UPPDPCTXT)
Check APN configuration across HSS, USN, UGW
Remove the existing subscriber session where required
Check the trace on the relevant PS Core nodes
Identify where the procedure fails or is rejected
Collect relevant evidence (traces, command outputs, screenshots)
Provide CHR / HC when requested by Huawei
